questions.stem: A major role of agriculture in the Nigerian economy is to

options.text: print the naira on behalf of the CBN
provide food, employment and industrial raw materials

questions.explanation: Agriculture feeds the population, occupies a large part of the labour force and supplies crops such as cotton, rubber and cassava to industry, as well as some export earnings. Currency issue, the MPR and deposit insurance are functions of monetary and financial institutions.

distractorRationale.a: Only the CBN issues the naira
distractorRationale.c: The MPR is set by the CBN, not by farmers
distractorRationale.d: NDIC, not agriculture, insures deposits

questions.stem: Since the 1970s, crude petroleum has been important to Nigeria mainly because it

options.text: employs most of the rural labour force on small farms
provides the bulk of export earnings and a large share of government revenue
is produced equally in every local government area
replaced the naira as legal tender

questions.explanation: Oil is an export and fiscal giant, not an employment giant. Most Nigerian workers remain in agriculture and informal services; production is concentrated in the Niger Delta, and the naira is still the legal tender issued by the CBN.

distractorRationale.a: Peasant agriculture, not oil, occupies most rural labour
distractorRationale.c: Oil production is geographically concentrated, which is part of the enclave problem
distractorRationale.d: The naira remains legal tender; oil is a commodity, not a currency

questions.stem: Dutch disease in the Nigerian context refers to

options.text: a plant infection that destroys cocoa trees
the crowding out of agriculture and manufacturing after an oil boom
the CBN's monopoly of note issue
a surplus budget caused by high VAT

questions.explanation: Dutch disease is the mechanism by which a booming oil sector and a strong or neglected non-oil tradable sector reduce the competitiveness of farms and factories. It is named after the Dutch gas boom, not after a crop disease, and it is unrelated to note issue or to VAT.

distractorRationale.a: The name is historical, not botanical; examiners want the economic mechanism
distractorRationale.c: Note issue is a CBN function and is not what Dutch disease means
distractorRationale.d: A VAT-driven surplus is a fiscal outcome, not Dutch disease

questions.stem: Which of the following is a problem of agriculture in Nigeria?

options.text: Inadequate storage facilities and poor rural infrastructure
The absence of any food crop in the country
The CBN's refusal to issue coins
A complete ban on peasant farming by the constitution

questions.explanation: Post-harvest losses from poor storage and the cost of moving crops on bad roads are standard, examinable problems, alongside land tenure, credit and climate. Nigeria grows many food crops, issues coins, and peasant farming is the dominant system, not a banned one.

distractorRationale.b: Nigeria produces staples such as cassava, yam, maize and rice; the problem is productivity and storage, not total absence
distractorRationale.c: Coin issue is unrelated to farm output
distractorRationale.d: There is no constitutional ban on peasant farming; smallholders are the backbone of the sector

questions.stem: Import substitution industrialisation aims to

options.text: replace imported consumer goods with locally produced ones, often behind tariffs
ban all manufacturing so as to import everything
replace the naira with a foreign currency
sell crude oil only to one foreign buyer

questions.explanation: ISI uses protection so that domestic factories can take the place of finished imports. Nigeria followed this path in textiles, assembly and brewing. It is the opposite of banning manufacturing, and it has nothing to do with currency substitution or a single oil buyer.

distractorRationale.b: That would be de-industrialisation, the reverse of ISI
distractorRationale.c: Dollarisation is an exchange-rate regime, not an industrial strategy
distractorRationale.d: Exclusive oil sales are a commercial-policy choice, not ISI

questions.stem: Nigeria's Structural Adjustment Programme of 1986 is best described as a shift towards

options.text: naira devaluation, fewer import licences, privatisation and trade liberalisation
a return to barter and the abolition of the CBN
higher tariffs on every import and a permanently fixed strong naira
the replacement of FAAC with a single military budget

questions.explanation: SAP tried to restore market prices: a cheaper naira, the dismantling of import-licence rent, privatisation of some public enterprises and more open trade, so that agriculture and industry would face world prices. It did not abolish money, and it moved away from, rather than towards, a strong-naira high-tariff regime.

distractorRationale.b: SAP operated inside a money economy; the CBN remained the monetary authority
distractorRationale.c: That package is closer to pre-SAP control and an overvalued naira, which SAP was designed to unwind
distractorRationale.d: FAAC and fiscal federalism continued; SAP was a macroeconomic and trade reform, not a rewriting of revenue allocation into one military budget

questions.stem: One of the primary challenges facing agriculture in Nigeria is

options.text: lack of available land for farming

questions.explanation: Inadequate access to modern technology significantly hampers agricultural productivity in Nigeria. Many farmers rely on traditional farming methods, which limits their yield and efficiency.

distractorRationale.a: While land availability can be an issue, it is not the primary challenge compared to technology access.
distractorRationale.b: Excessive rainfall is not a common problem; rather, irregular rainfall patterns are more prevalent.
distractorRationale.d: High levels of agricultural exports are not a challenge but rather a goal for the sector.
